name: Ukrainian Borscht
description: Borscht is genuinely rooted in Ukraine, tracing back to the early Kyivan Rus era, though it's since spread and been adapted across the wider Slavic world. Real technique never skips cooking the tomato paste an extra minute or two until it visibly darkens and turns aromatic, since this real step builds the soup's depth; the beets are cut into uniform matchsticks for even cooking and color, and real tradition tastes and balances the finished soup with a splash of vinegar and a pinch of sugar right at the end.
steps_detailed: Simmer the beef in 4 cups water 40-45 minutes until nearly tender.
Cook the onion and carrot in a little oil, 4-5 minutes, then add the tomato paste and cook 1-2 minutes more until it visibly darkens and turns aromatic - real technique never skips this real step.
Add the beets, potato, and this mixture to the broth, and simmer 20 minutes.
Add the cabbage and garlic, and simmer 10-12 minutes more until everything is tender.
Stir in the vinegar and sugar, tasting and adjusting to balance real sweet against real tart.
Stir in the dill and serve topped with the sour cream.

name: Ukrainian Varenyky
description: Varenyky, dumplings just as beloved as borscht in Ukraine, genuinely vary by region - real Polissia versions use crushed beans, Zakarpattia leans on cheese, and Chernihiv adds real bacon crisps, reflecting real regional identity rather than one fixed recipe.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and egg with a little water into a smooth, elastic dough. Rest 15 minutes.
Mix the mashed potato with the cottage cheese and raw onion for the filling.
Roll the dough thin and cut into rounds, fill each with a spoonful of filling, and fold and pinch the edges firmly to seal.
Boil in salted water 4-5 minutes until they float.
Toss with the melted butter before serving.

name: Ukrainian Holubtsi (Stuffed Cabbage)
description: Holubtsi, cabbage leaves stuffed with rice and meat, is a genuine Ukrainian staple, real technique using well-softened, pliable cabbage leaves so they roll without tearing.
steps_detailed: Blanch the cabbage leaves 3-4 minutes until fully pliable.
Mix the raw rice with the beef and onion.
Roll a spoonful of the filling tightly into each cabbage leaf.
Arrange in a pot, cover with the tomatoes and enough water to just cover, and simmer 40-45 minutes until the rice is tender.

name: Ukrainian Deruny (Potato Pancakes)
description: Deruny, crispy grated potato pancakes, are a beloved Ukrainian dish, real technique squeezing excess liquid from the grated potato so they fry crisp.
steps_detailed: Squeeze the grated potato and onion well to remove excess liquid.
Mix with the flour and egg.
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil and fry, flattening slightly, 3-4 minutes per side, until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Ukrainian Beet and Herring Salad (Shuba)
description: Shuba, a real layered beet and fish salad, is a beloved Ukrainian holiday dish, real technique layering the ingredients in a specific order so the beet's color bleeds through as the finishing layer.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Fish, sardine, Atlantic, canned in oil, drained solids with bone

ingredients.ingredient: Fish, sardine, Atlantic, canned in oil, drained solids with bone

steps_detailed: Layer the grated potato, flaked fish, and grated beet in a dish, spreading a thin layer of mayonnaise between each.
Chill at least 1 hour before serving, so the beet color bleeds through the top layer.

name: Ukrainian Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with dill and lemon, reflecting Ukraine's rich Dnieper River and Black Sea fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the dill and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Ukrainian Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Ukraine.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Ukrainian Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Ukrainian home cooking outside the specific named dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.

description: A simple dill and sour cream sauce, a common Ukrainian condiment for varenyky and potatoes.
